title: The State of Independent Restaurant Websites 2026
note: Aggregates computed from automated scans. No individual site is identified.
attribution: Free to use and cite under CC BY 4.0. Credit Clikiti with a link.
citation: Clikiti. (2026, October 15). The state of independent restaurant websites 2026 (Q4 2026) [Report]. https://clikiti.com/research/restaurants/2026-q4
audience: Web agencies and freelancers selling to independent restaurants, cafés and bars
findings: Only 29% of the 180 independent restaurant, café and bar websites we scanned mark allergens or vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free dishes.
A typical site answers four of the eight questions diners ask before choosing (mean 4).
The median overall score is 78 out of 100 (mean 78).
The least-answered questions are "Can I eat here with my allergy or diet?" (29%), "What will it cost?" (34%) and "Can I get a table without calling?" (37%).
The best-answered are "Are you open tonight?" (77%) and "Where are you, and where do I park?" (71%).
Cafés and bakeries have the highest median score (81), against 79 for bars and brewpubs, 78 for casual and family restaurants and 77 for chef-driven and fine dining.
84% fail "Restaurant, café or bar structured data" (Schema.org · FoodEstablishment).
26% fail "Loads in under 2.5 s on a phone" (Core Web Vitals · LCP).
Chef-driven places book online more often than cafés.

technical.label: Restaurant, café or bar structured data
Loads in under 2.5 s on a phone

agencyProblems.label: Restaurant, café or bar structured data
agencyProblems.fix: Add Restaurant (or CafeOrCoffeeShop, BarOrPub) structured data with address, hours, menu link and booking link.
agencyProblems.pitch: Search engines and assistants have to guess your hours and where your menu is.

agencyProblems.label: Allergens or vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free dishes marked
agencyProblems.question: Can I eat here with my allergy or diet?
agencyProblems.fix: Mark vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free dishes on the menu, with a short allergen note on how the kitchen handles requests.
agencyProblems.pitch: A guest with an allergy picks the place that says so before they arrive; the server answers the same question every night.

agencyProblems.label: Prices shown on the menu
agencyProblems.question: What will it cost?
agencyProblems.fix: Show the price beside every dish on the menu page.
agencyProblems.pitch: Diners choose where to eat on what it will cost, and the menu makes them guess.

agencyProblems.label: Text contrast passes 4.5:1
agencyProblems.fix: Raise text contrast to at least 4.5:1 in the theme, especially text over food photos.
agencyProblems.pitch: Parts of the site are hard to read, and it is a WCAG failure.

agencyProblems.label: Book a table online, or a clear walk-ins-only note
agencyProblems.question: Can I get a table without calling?
agencyProblems.fix: A "Book a table" button on every page, linked to the booking system, or a plain line saying the place is walk-ins only.
agencyProblems.pitch: A table for Friday means a phone call during service, so people book somewhere else.
